store-sequence alignment (str/strb/strh instructions only, aligned like the bl-sequence compass) found the true shape of the 43-instruction store deficit: the reference spills specifically r4 to [sp,#8] 27 times (24 reloads) across the whole function body, ours does this only ~1-3 times. Verified this is NOT one persistent value stuck needing constant respill (the one candidate constant checked, 0x080AF28C, appears exactly once in both builds' pools) -- it is -fcall-used-r4 (a project build flag making r4 caller-saved) combined with the register allocator choosing r4 for many DIFFERENT short-lived cross-call values throughout the reference, where our build's allocator picks other (callee-saved, no-respill-needed) registers for the equivalent values. This is a global allocation-PRIORITY difference, not a locatable single-site bug -- the same 'measured, not locally reachable' class as 080bbb0c's scheduler-tie residual, but spanning the whole function rather than one instruction pair. No source-level lever for this was found or attempted to be forced this session; it would need the same allocno-priority-dump instrument that worked for 080bbb0c's final pair, applied at much larger scale (many pseudos, not one).
